script.base: Books have a one-score game, TB 22.8 to ATL 20.8, so neither side is a blowout or a pass-funnel (spread is only 2, under the 3.5 flag). TB leans on Bucky Irving (64 carries, 317 yards over weeks 5-7) to stay in front late; ATL stays in it with Penix throwing to London (31 targets, 246 yards, 348 air) and Pitts (18/124/68 air) while Bijan still gets a full but not spike workload (46 carries, 210 rush yards plus 14 targets, 69 rec yards). Pace is moderate on a 43.5, not a London-style shootout and not a weather slog.
script.flip1: TB jumps ahead early, Irving soaks the clock, and ATL abandons the run so Bijan's rush and rush+rec lines die while Pitts/London/Dotson targets rise on checkdowns into a 41% TB blitz.
script.flip2: ATL grabs the lead and feeds Bijan the way the older 145-rush / 147 rush+rec game did, or both defenses drag it into a sub-43.5 slog and every receiving over stalls.

injury_fallout: Official pre-game injury report in the pack (nflverse) lists nobody out, doubtful, or limited on either side, so there is no next-man-up carry or target shift to price. matchup.shell: MOFO/MOFC and man/zone rates are not in the pack, so no coverage shell is claimed. Proxy only: TB blitzes 41% and ATL blitzes 25%. Both defenses bleed the middle (TB middle YPA 9.53 on 49 attempts; ATL middle YPA 9.76 on 41) and are tighter outside (TB left 6.04/100, right 5.95/95; ATL left 6.38/118, right 5.93/126).
matchup.pressure: TB blitz 41% is the pressure look. ATL EPA/db is -0.02 vs blitz and -0.16 vs no blitz, so the blitz does not crush Atlanta and checkdowns can survive. ATL blitzes only 25%; TB EPA/db is -0.18 vs blitz and -0.14 vs none, a small blitz dip that Atlanta does not force often. No time-to-throw, sack, or individual rusher charting is in the pack.
matchup.bleeds: TB run defense is the stingy side: 3.87 YPC, 14 runs of 10+ and 16 passes of 20+ for 260 yards over 7 games. The pass bleed is the middle, not the perimeter. ATL allows 4.05 YPC, the same 14 runs of 10+, and more explosives (23 passes of 20+ for 302). Egbuka's 25 targets for only 86 yards and 207 air is the inefficient deep profile; he is not on an available priced prop.
matchup.overlap: Pitts is the overlap: 68 air yards on 18 targets is a short/intermediate TE, which is exactly where TB's 9.53 middle YPA lives, and Atlanta's near-flat EPA vs a 41% blitz keeps that hook/middle alive. London's 348 air yards attack the perimeter, where TB YPA is about 6.0, so he is not the overlap. Bijan's rush side runs into 3.87 YPC, not into a soft front.
